artifacts.purpose: Utility module providing contextual phrases for physics metrics (speed, acceleration, mass ratio)

pipelines.summary: Created metricContext.ts utility module with three context phrase functions. All threshold values are defined as named constants at the top of the file for easy tuning. getSpeedContext() provides five speed ranges from 'very slow — heavy hauler' to 'extremely fast — possibly unbalanced'. getAccelerationContext() provides four acceleration ranges from 'sluggish response' to 'fighter-like responsiveness'. getMassRatioContext() provides four mass ratio ranges from 'minimal mass increase' to 'extreme — may feel unresponsive'. All functions accept shipSize parameter for future refinement.

comments.note: metricContext.ts - All threshold constants are clearly named and grouped at the top of the file with section comments. No magic numbers in function logic. Easy to tune values without touching business logic.

Context phrases are concise and intuitive for X4 players. Speed ranges cover typical ship classes (hauler, freighter, corvette, fighter). Acceleration phrases describe handling feel. Mass ratio phrases warn about impact on responsiveness.

Functions accept shipSize parameter even though currently unused. This provides forward compatibility if we want to refine context phrases per ship size class later. TypeScript strict mode satisfied with explicit types.

comments.description: TypeScript compilation error TS6133: Parameter 'shipSize' is declared but never used in getSpeedContext() and getAccelerationContext() functions. This violates TypeScript strict mode under noUnusedParameters rule.
comments.fix: Add underscore prefix to indicate intentional unused parameter: '_shipSize: string'. Or add @ts-expect-error comment with explanation if parameter is reserved for future use.

pipelines.summary: WP-005 FAILED QA validation. TypeScript compilation fails under strict mode due to unused 'shipSize' parameter in two functions (lines 43, 66). While the implementation comment states the parameter is 'available for future refinement', TypeScript strict mode with noUnusedParameters enabled treats this as an error. Fix required: prefix parameter with underscore (_shipSize) to indicate intentional non-use, or add @ts-expect-error directive.

artifacts.purpose: Fixed TypeScript strict mode errors by prefixing unused shipSize parameters with underscore

pipelines.summary: Fixed TypeScript compilation errors in metricContext.ts. Changed 'shipSize' parameter to '_shipSize' in both getSpeedContext() and getAccelerationContext() functions (lines 43, 66). This follows TypeScript convention for intentionally unused parameters and satisfies noUnusedParameters rule in strict mode. Parameter remains available for future refinement without triggering compilation errors. Verified: npx tsc --noEmit passes cleanly.

comments.note: Underscore prefix is the idiomatic TypeScript approach for 'intentionally unused but available for future use' parameters. More elegant than @ts-expect-error comments and clearly signals intent to future developers.

comments.description: Verified fix: Both getSpeedContext() and getAccelerationContext() now use _shipSize parameter prefix. TypeScript strict mode noUnusedParameters rule satisfied.

comments.description: All threshold constants are clearly named and grouped at the top of the file with section comments. No magic numbers in function logic. Excellent maintainability - thresholds can be tuned without touching business logic.

Underscore prefix on _shipSize parameters is the idiomatic TypeScript approach for 'intentionally unused but available for future use'. Satisfies noUnusedParameters rule while keeping parameter for future refinement.

Context phrases are concise, intuitive, and appropriate for X4 Foundations players. Speed ranges cover typical ship classes (hauler→freighter→corvette→fighter). Acceleration phrases describe handling feel. Mass ratio phrases warn about responsiveness impact.
Function logic uses clear if/else chains with threshold comparisons. Each range has explicit boundaries. Return values are string literals - no complex string building. Very readable.

File structure is exemplary: constants section at top, function exports below. JSDoc comments explain purpose and parameters. TypeScript strict mode satisfied with explicit parameter types and return type inference.
Pure functions with no side effects. No external dependencies. No DOM manipulation. No eval or code execution. Completely safe utility module.
O(1) complexity for all functions - simple threshold comparisons. No loops, recursion, or expensive operations. Will execute in <1ms even with thousands of calls. Perfect performance.
